# Staff job-applicant specialization mechanic

## Problem statement

Main Street currently has a single staff mechanic: staff cards that go into the player's hand and passively expand hand capacity (`handSlotsAdded`). There is no in-game staff that is employed at a specific deployed business and grants that business a passive specialization buff. This item adds that new staff mechanic.

## Users

- **Main Street player** — wants more meaningful decisions when hiring staff: choosing where to place an applicant, weighing passive buffs, and taking on per-turn salary costs.
- **Game designer** — wants a reusable, deterministic staff-applicant mechanic that works with existing staff templates and can be extended with new applicant cards later.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Applicant trigger:** Each turn there is a per-turn chance that a staff member applies for work at one of the deployed businesses on the street. The chance is computed as `(reputation + income per turn)%`, capped at 15%. The applicant targets a deployed business that has a free employment slot (one staff slot per business level).
2. **Passive specialization buff:** Each staff member grants a passive, always-on buff to the business at which they are employed. Skills are assigned from a specialization pool and are randomized **once per game** at game start, remaining locked for the full game; a staff member's skill is disconnected from its nominal job (e.g. a "Baker" can carry a "Town Gossip" skill). At a minimum the "Town Gossip" skill is implemented, firing the existing once-per-turn peek mechanic (see CG-0MSXOW6GN008ZSMN).
3. **Hire / decline flow:** The applicant is presented as a new card type that **walks on from the left** of the screen. The player either lets it walk off to the right (decline) or hires it (walks into the hand / is employed). Hiring costs **no immediate coins** but adds an ongoing per-turn salary cost (deducted alongside existing staff/community-space ongoing costs during the income phase, clamped at 0 coins).
4. **Capacity & let-go economics:** A business can employ one staff member per business level (level 1 = 1 slot, etc.). The player can let a staff member go (lay off), which costs 1 turn's salary and 1 reputation.
5. **Tests & docs:** The mechanic is covered by unit tests (deterministic trigger under seeded RNG, passive-buff application, hire/decline, let-go penalties, per-level slot enforcement) and a browser/scene test for the walk-on/walk-off presentation. All related documentation is updated (code comments, README/wiki docs entries as applicable). Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Staff applicants for this mechanic are **distinct** from the existing hand-slot staff cards (`handSlotsAdded` mechanic) — they do not go into the player's hand as hand cards; they are employed at a deployed business.
- Applicant pool starts from existing staff templates; add new applicant cards via the follow-up work item CG-0MT1CIWSD003VBPK (not scope here).
- Passive buffs are applied per-business; must not conflict with existing per-slot `currentIncome` / `currentReputationPerTurn` caching in `applyIncome`.
- New card presentation must follow SLL positioning and the shared HandView/PileView / animation + SFX conventions per AGENTS.md (rule 8, `COMMON_SFX_KEYS`, reduced-motion respected).

## Existing state

- `StaffCard` interface in `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` (familly: 'staff') with `handSlotsAdded`, `reputationPerTurn`, `refreshCostDiscount`, `actionsPerTurn`. Staff templates loaded from `card-data.csv` (`_STAFF_CARD_TEMPLATES`).
- `MainStreetState.ts`: `streetGrid` of deployed businesses/community-spaces; `staffCards[]` (hand-slot staff) + `staffCardMarket[]`; business cards carry `maxLevel`/`level`.
- `MainStreetEngine.ts`: `hireStaffCard()` (hand-slot hire), `layOffStaffCard()` (hand-slot layoff), `executeDayStart()` resets per-turn state; `applyIncome()` in `MainStreetAdjacency.ts` deducts staff + community-space ongoing costs and applies per-slot income/rep.
- Related peek skill work: CG-0MSXOW6GN008ZSMN (implement staff peek skill), CG-0MSXOWLHU0099QF6 (face-down deck rendering).

## Desired change

Introduce a per-turn staff-applicant phase/step in the turn loop: roll the applicant chance, when triggered pick a deployed business with a free employment slot and spawn an applicant card that walks on from the left. On hire, employ the applicant at that business, add its passive specialization buff to the business's income/rep/synergy computations, and register its ongoing salary cost. On decline, walk the card off to the right with no effect. Add per-level employment-slot tracking, and a let-go action costing 1 turn's salary + 1 reputation.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — new state: applicant presentation state, per-business employment slots, employed-applicant list.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — new applicant-trigger step, hire/decline/let-go actions, ongoing-cost integration; `resolveIncident`-style applicant chance roll.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacency.ts` — apply passive specialization buffs per-business in `applyIncome` (+ currentReputationPerTurn).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` — applicant/specialization skill type definitions (start with existing templates + Town Gossip skill).
- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — Town Gossip skill / any new specialization columns if added.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` + `MainStreetAnimator.ts` — new card type walk-on (from left) / walk-off (right) / walk-into-hand animation + SFX.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` / `MainStreetCommands.ts` — hire/decline input + command wiring.
- `tests/main-street/` — unit + browser tests for the mechanic.

## Related work

- CG-0MSXOW6GN008ZSMN — Implement staff peek skill ("Town Gossip" active peek).
- CG-0MSXOXN81004MW8I — Add peek once-per-turn unit tests.
- CG-0MT1CIWSD003VBPK — Staff specialization: new applicant card suggestions (follow-up, out of scope here).
- CG-0MSQJ7VL9009JHF4 — Group F: Staff abilities beyond hand slots.
- CG-0MS9HJ6AL0087DPB — Engine: ongoingCost for community spaces (same ongoing-cost deduction path).

## Clarifying questions & answers (Appendix)

- Q: How frequently does a staff member apply? — Answer (producer): Per-turn chance computed as `(reputation + income per turn)%`, capped at 15%. Source: interactive reply 2026-08-20, recorded in comment CG-C0MT1CHYML001OOU8.
- Q: Are specializations passive or active? — Answer (producer): Passive, always-on buff applied to the business at which they are employed. Source: interactive reply 2026-08-20.
- Q: When is the specialization randomized? — Answer (producer): Once per game at start, locked for the full game. Source: interactive reply 2026-08-20.
- Q: Which staff pool for applicants? — Answer (producer): Start with existing staff templates; create a follow-up work item for new card suggestions. → Created CG-0MT1CIWSD003VBPK. Source: interactive reply 2026-08-20.
- Q: How is the applicant presented in the UI? — Answer (producer): New card type that walks on from the left, then either walks off to the right (decline) or walks into the hand (hire). Source: interactive reply 2026-08-20.
- Q: What is the specific applicant trigger rate? — Answer (producer): `(Reputation + income per turn)%` capped at 15%. Open detail: the "Town Gossip" example in the original description describes an *active* peek to the top 3 cards of the upcoming deck, which conflicts with the producer's "passive" answer — resolved as passive buff with the active peek delegated to the existing peek skill (CG-0MSXOW6GN008ZSMN). Source: interactive reply 2026-08-20 + item description.

---

## Related work (automated report — find_related)

- **CG-0MLSDXY9F1FSGQ38** – Coloretto (set-building tableau) (completed)
- **CG-0MSRGUM4P009XRM3** – Upgrade level-up burst on target business (completed)
- **CG-0MSTB03U6009J2WV** – Main Street: clicking a tutorial button should not pass through to the cards below (completed)

## Goal (user story)

As a Main Street player, I want to play a competitive mode against an AI opponent who builds businesses on the **same street**, so that turns give me more to do and the game has a rival to race against.

## Design scope (from feasibility analysis, 2025-07 session)

- **Shared street grid** (10 slots); each placed business is owned by one player; income from a business accrues to its **owner**.
- **Events affect the whole street**: investment events and incidents keep the existing street-wide resolution semantics, but income/damage must be routed per-owner.
- **Staff are player-only**: the AI does not hire staff, and its competitive decision space excludes staff actions (hire-staff, peek).
- **Single shared market row**: buying a card denies it to the opponent (market competition is a first-class feature).
- **Alternating turn structure** — design decision to confirm at intake: alternate MarketPhases within a shared day vs. alternating full days.

## Reusability findings (basis for this item)

- The decision layer (`MainStreetAiStrategy`, `GreedyStrategy`, `scoreAction`, `enumerateLegalActions`, `MainStreetAiPlayer`) transfers ~1:1 — it is UI-free and already shared between the Monte Carlo harness and the hint system.
- The state/engine layers are single-owner: `MainStreetState` has one resourceBank/hand/staffCards/actionsRemaining; `applyIncome`, `resolveEvent`, `resolveIncident`, `computeScore`, `checkEndConditions` all assume one owner. These need a per-player split plus owner-tagged grid slots.
- Greedy heuristics assume the AI owns the whole street (`scoreBusinessAction = (income+synergy)*horizon - cost`; `aiPlanningHorizon` reads a single score) — scoring must become ownership-aware.
- PRD M3 (`docs/main-street/prd-milestone-3.md`) explicitly scoped "AI vs. player (competitive mode)" as N/A — this item is a deliberate scope extension; note it in the PRD.

## Acceptance criteria (proposed)

- AC1: A competitive-mode state model exists with per-player coins/reputation, hand, staff, action budget and score, plus owner-tagged street slots; deterministic and replayable via seeded RNG.
- AC2: The AI opponent plays a legal full turn through the existing strategy layer (`enumerateLegalActions` → scored choice → `executeAction`), with staff actions excluded.
- AC3: Income accrues to the owner of each business; street-wide events/incidents affect both players under the shared-street semantics.
- AC4: A head-to-head Monte Carlo harness (extending `MainStreetMonteCarlo`) measures the win distribution across >=200 seeds to validate competitive balance.
- AC5 (scene, may be split into a child at planning): competitive mode is selectable from the game selector, renders the shared street with owner colouring, alternates turns, and animates AI turns with SFX per the audio/feedback rule (AGENTS.md best practice 8).
data.title: Main Street competitive mode: AI opponent on the shared street

## Goal (user story)

As a developer of the competitive mode, I want the balancing AI's decision layer (`MainStreetAiStrategy` / `GreedyStrategy` / `scoreAction` / `MainStreetAiPlayer`) adapted to shared-street competitive semantics, so the opponent plays competently on a street it does not fully own.

## Context

The existing heuristics assume the AI owns the whole street:
- `scoreBusinessAction` / `scorePlayBusinessFromHandAction` value `(income + synergy) * horizon - cost` with no ownership concept.
- `aiPlanningHorizon` measures distance to the win threshold via `computeScore`, which sums a single player's coins + reputation.
- `enumerateLegalActions` includes staff actions (`hire-staff`, `peek-incident-deck`) — competitive mode makes staff player-only.

Parent: Main Street competitive mode epic (CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30).

## Scope

- Ownership-aware scoring: evaluate income, synergy, and horizon against the **AI's own** resources/businesses and its own win threshold.
- Staff exclusion: competitive-mode action enumeration drops staff actions from the AI's option space.
- Deterministic validation: extend `MainStreetMonteCarlo` (or a sibling harness) to run head-to-head AI-vs-AI and, where feasible, AI-vs-baseline matches across >=200 seeds; document win/score distributions.

## Out of scope (decision to record in item)

Whether to add opponent-aware *denial* reasoning (blocking the opponent's best slot, buying to deny) — record an explicit in/out decision with rationale; denial can be a follow-up child if in.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: `scoreAction` and the per-type scoring helpers evaluate placement/upgrade/event value using only the acting player's resources and owned businesses, with the planning horizon computed from the acting player's own score vs. their win threshold.
- AC2: Competitive-mode legal-action enumeration excludes `hire-staff` and staff-skill actions (peek), while the shared single-player enumeration is unchanged.
- AC3: A deterministic head-to-head Monte Carlo harness runs the adapted strategy against a baseline over >=200 seeds and produces win/score distribution metrics (extension of `MainStreetMonteCarloMetrics` or equivalent).
- AC4: All existing single-player AI tests (ai-strategy, hint consistency, balance guardrails) still pass unchanged.
data.title: Competitive AI strategy: ownership-aware, staff-free scoring for shared-street play

# Intake Brief: Florist provides no income (CG-0MT6EQSPW002E7RC)

## Problem statement

The Florist business card (`biz-florist`) does not provide meaningful income: it sat at `baseIncome=0` in `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` (a placeholder never filled in), and although a partial rebalance (CG-0MSVYPEZ90085SHE) raised it to 3.0 on 2026-08-24, the card remains materially weaker than its tier-5 peers (net income 1.75/turn vs 2.25 for Cinema / Juice Bar) with no regression protection. Producer decision: **rebalance** the Florist properly; **no backward compatibility** needed for old saves.

## Users

- **Main Street players** — expect every purchasable business card to produce income commensurate with its cost and tier; a tier-5 card that under-earns feels broken.
  - User story: "As a Main Street player, I open/buy a Florist (cost 5, tier 5) and expect it to earn income on par with other tier-5 businesses (Cinema, Juice Bar) so the Commerce–Culture bridge is worth buying."
- **Balancers / developers** — need a regression guard so business templates never silently carry `baseIncome=0` again.
  - User story: "As a balancer, I add or edit a business card in `card-data.csv` and an automated test tells me immediately if it provides no income (unless deliberately rep-only, like Clinic)."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Rebalanced income:** The Florist (`biz-florist`) defines a positive base income at tier-5 parity in `card-data.csv` — proposed `baseIncome=3.5` (net **≥ 2.0/turn** after the 1.25 ongoing cost; peer net is 2.25). Verified by runtime `computeBusinessIncome` on a solo placement.
2. **Income actually credited:** A unit test places a Florist solo on the street grid and asserts the end-of-turn `IncomeResult` includes the slot with positive total and coins increase by at least the tier-parity baseline.
3. **Regression protection:** A template-wide test asserts every business card template has `baseIncome > 0` except intentionally rep-only cards (only `biz-clinic` today), and an explicit Florist test locks in the rebalanced value.
4. **Display:** The Florist's card face and market/tooltip labels show a non-zero income ("Income: +X/turn") — the SVG generator already keys off `baseIncome`, so this is covered by the data + existing display tests.
5. **Docs + suite:** All related documentation updated (`docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` income/ongoing columns; `docs/main-street/prd-balance-process-and-tooling.md` drops the stale "Florist = zero base income" example at line 236); full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- No legacy-save compatibility required (producer decision): change `card-data.csv` freely; old checkpoint saves may keep pre-change values by design (`loadTemplatesFromCsv` trusts checkpoint CSV).
- Preserve the Florist's identity: tier 5, cost 5, `Commerce|Culture` bridge, `+0.1 rep/turn`, and the Garden Center upgrade path (`upg-garden-center`: cost 7, +2 income, +1 synergy range, +1 reputation) must remain coherent with the rebalanced base.
- TCE conventions: data-first change in `card-data.csv`; engine/game code untouched unless tests expose a real bug; docs updated in the same change per the doc-update policy.

## Existing state

- `card-data.csv` florist row (both `dev` and `main` since 2026-08-24): `baseIncome=3.0`, `reputationPerTurn=0.1`, `ongoingCost=1.25`, tier 5, `Commerce|Culture`.
- Runtime verified on current `dev`: solo `computeBusinessIncome` = 3.0; rep +0.1; synergy rate defaults to 0.5 (parity with most bridge cards — both `synergyCoinBonus`/`synergyRepBonus` empty is not florist-specific).
- No test locks florist income: `tests/main-street/expanded-card-pool.test.ts` asserts synergy types only; `balance-cards.test.ts` skips cards with falsy `baseIncome`.
- Stale doc: `docs/main-street/prd-balance-process-and-tooling.md:236` still cites Florist as a "zero base income" example.

## Desired change

- Rebalance the Florist in `card-data.csv` to tier-5 parity (proposed `baseIncome=3.5`; net 2.25/turn after ongoing cost — exact value tuned in planning, but AC1 locks the floor).
- Add regression tests (template-wide `baseIncome > 0` guard + explicit Florist income/crediting tests).
- Update the stale docs references.

**Key Files:**
- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — florist `baseIncome` rebalance (primary change)
- `tests/main-street/expanded-card-pool.test.ts` — existing Florist synergy test; add income assertions
- `tests/main-street/balance-cards.test.ts` — add/extend template-wide `baseIncome > 0` guard for business cards (rep-only exceptions)
- `tests/main-street/income-phase-data.test.ts` — end-of-turn Florist income crediting test (IncomeResult includes the slot; coins increase)
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` — Florist income/ongoing columns
- `docs/main-street/prd-balance-process-and-tooling.md` — remove stale zero-income Florist example (line 236)

## Related work

- **CG-0MSVYPEZ90085SHE** («Main Street: business cards incur ongoing per-turn cost…») — completed; the rebalance that first moved Florist 0 → 3.0 (commit `257c6298`).
- **CG-0MT3IPFSF005KEFB** («Evaluate synergy-type distribution across Main Street tiers») — completed; tier/synergy context for bridge cards.
- **CG-0MSQE2NLX003ADIY** («Main Street: design 50+ new cards of varying types») — completed; source of the expanded pool incl. Florist.
- **CG-0MRV84ZT60069PW6** («Per-card incremental income/reputation tracking») — completed; the `currentIncome` cache that `applyIncome` reads.
- **CG-0MTDEEUWI0079IOV** («Tests + documentation») — blocked; template-wide test/docs hygiene context (find-related).
- **CG-0MP4189FQ001USVY** («Headless Smoke for All Scenes») — completed; display/headless verification context (find-related).

> Related-work report generated by `/skill:find-related` (`.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-CG-0MT6EQSPW002E7RC.md`).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Reproduction basis: Was the 'no income' observation from a game/save started before 2026-08-24 (pre-rebalance)? Current dev appears fixed (3.0/turn, verified). Is there any still-reproducible symptom on current dev — or is the fix sufficient?" — Answer (producer): "The card itself shows no income regardless of the game. Likely says 0 in the CSV." Evidence: current `dev` and `main` both define `baseIncome=3.0`; runtime verified 3.0/turn. Interpretation: the reported symptom matches the pre-fix data state; the answer is treated as a directive to rebalance rather than evidence of an active defect on current builds. Research: `card-data.csv` + `MainStreetCards.ts` CSV parse + `computeBusinessIncome`/`applyIncome` inspected; diff `257c6298` shown in git history.
- Q2: "Scope if fixed: accept regression test + stale-doc fix then close, or is a re-balance/redesign of the Florist preferred instead?" — Answer (producer): "rebalance."
- Q3: "Legacy saves: migrate/override saved florist income, or is 'start a new game' acceptable (current by-design behaviour)?" — Answer (producer): "no need for backward compat."

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — target value:** `baseIncome=3.5` is proposed as tier-5 parity (Cinema/Juice Bar); the exact number is a plan-stage tuning decision. AC1 locks only the floor (net ≥ 2.0/turn).
- **Assumption — data-only fix:** the defect is in `card-data.csv`; no engine bug is expected. If runtime tests expose one (e.g., a placement path that never caches `currentIncome`), that becomes part of the fix.
- **Risk — producer symptom may predate the current build:** the producer's "no income" observation cannot be reproduced on current `dev`/`main` (3.0 verified). Mitigation: AC2's end-of-turn runtime test proves income is credited on the current build.
- **Risk — baked snapshots:** rebalancing florist data may affect Monte Carlo transcripts, E2E recordings, or tests with hardcoded florist values; the full suite must pass before `in_review`.
- **Assumption — carried-over saves:** checkpoint-saved games keep pre-change florist data by design (`loadTemplatesFromCsv` trusts checkpoint CSV); accepted per "no backward compat".
- **Scope-creep guard:** opportunities noticed during intake — data-wide synergy-consistency review (most bridge cards have empty `synergyCoinBonus` values), rebalancing other under-power cards, updating historical playtest-scenario numbers — are intentionally **out of scope**; file separate work items if wanted.

## Headline

Rebalance the Florist business card to tier-5 income parity (currently net 1.75/turn vs 2.25 for Cinema/Juice Bar), add regression tests so no business template can silently carry zero income again, and fix the stale docs that still cite the Florist as a zero-income card.

Intake Brief: Follow-up to CG-0MTCP76MP0088TQW

The cash-line overlay fix (Cash: +X / -Y) is complete, but the original per-turn cost text baked into the card SVG face is still visible.

## Problem Statement

1. **Baked cost text remains:** Business/community-space card SVGs still bake the orange (#ff8844) \`-X/turn\` ongoing-cost label into the card face (static SVGs under public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/ via scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs, plus the runtime CSV-fallback generator MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.generateCardSvgFromCsvRow and test-facing generateBusinessCardSvg). The user wants this redundant baked label removed now that the overlay cash line shows the cost.
2. **Two-tone cash line:** The overlay cash line \`Cash: +2 / -0.75\` is currently monochrome (#dddd44 yellow when both present, #44ff44 green otherwise). The user wants income in green and expenses in red.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The baked orange (-X/turn) cost text is removed from the business/community-space card face in: static SVGs (public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/), scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs, and MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts (generateBusinessCardSvg + generateCardSvgFromCsvRow business/community-space branches).
2. The static card SVGs are regenerated (script update + asset regeneration) so the shipped faces have no baked cost text.
3. The overlay cash line renders income in green and ongoing cost in red on the same line (Format stays \`Cash: +X / -Y\`; e.g. \`Cash: +2 / -0.75\` with +2 green, -0.75 red). The \`Cash:\`/\`/\` separator may remain neutral.
4. Staff cards (staff-*) keep their baked -X/turn cost text (no overlay pipeline for staff; it is their only cost display).
5. Existing tests updated and new tests added for: no baked cost text in generated SVGs, two-tone cash line segments.
6. Full project test suite passes (npm test) and build succeeds (npm run build).
7. Docs updated (docs/DEVELOPER.md overlay pipeline section, CHANGELOG) to reflect the two-tone cash line and removal of the baked cost text.

## Key Files

- scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs (remove ongoingCostText)
- public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/*.svg (regenerated)
- example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts (generateBusinessCardSvg, generateCardSvgFromCsvRow)
- example-games/main-street/scenes/UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts (cashLine segment colors)
- example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts (applyUpgradeOverlays segment rendering)
- tests/main-street/cash-line-overlay.test.ts, business-ongoing-cost.test.ts, card-svg-generator.test.ts
- docs/DEVELOPER.md

## Notes / Decisions Needed

- Segment rendering: extend OverlayTextSpec or add a segments array so applyUpgradeOverlays draws income green + cost red side by side, horizontally centred as a group.
- Uncertain: exact neutral colour for 'Cash:'/'/' text and exact red hue. Proposal: neutral #dddddd, red #ff6644 (matching the baked colour family), green #44ff44 (existing).

## Related Work

- Supersedes part of CG-0MTCP76MP0088TQW (cost per turn on cards overlays income) whose implementer noted the baked text as follow-up work.
- Related: CG-0MSVYPEZ90085SHE (ongoing cost mechanic), CG-0MRCQL9KO007SUUJ (Income: prefix).
